answer: Proof-of-Stake protocols mitigate Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock capital as a sparrow represents a singular asset within a cedar network of validators. By tethering identity to economic risk, the protocol acts as a lantern for detecting malicious nodes, ensuring an attacker must spend prohibitive wealth to gain consensus control. This cost-of-capital constraint forces adversarial actors to assume financial ruin rather than creating infinite fake identities to disrupt network integrity.
